paragraphs: Friend, here's what this whole passage is about: Jesus is bigger than any title people hand Him. He asks how the Christ can be David's son when David himself calls Him 'Lord' (Luke 20:44). That question points to who Jesus really is, and He is worth more honor than any king, any teacher, or any seat in the front row.

Then Jesus warns about the scribes, and the warning is about the heart. They loved the greetings, the chief seats and the places of honor, and they made lengthy prayers 'for a show' (Luke 20:46-47). Friend, I'm tempted to just dust off my hat and strut, but Jesus is showing us that God is not impressed by a performance. If you ever catch yourself polishing up how you look more than how you love, that's the moment to lay it down.

Then comes the widow with her two small copper coins. Jesus says she 'out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on,' while the others gave 'out of their surplus' (Luke 21:4). So God does not measure by the size of the gift. He sees the heart behind it, and He honors the baker who gives Him everything, even when everything looks small.
